answer: A bounty turns a sybil gang against itself. Any agent may report a fake identity; once verified, its stake is confiscated and 40 percent goes to the reporter. The seized record keeps a pigment mark linking identities from the same funds, so the gang cannot relaunch under fresh names. A silent member risks being reported on the next voyage, while a defector keeps the bounty. No harbor shields a reported stake, so the gang must pay hush money per member per recruit. For 1,000 fakes it must fund 1,000 stakes plus hush payments growing per recruit; an honest agent stakes once.
